aggressive_definition: Advanced-stage prostate cancer; the abstract does not provide a specific stage threshold.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: After controlling for multiple testing, 12 glycerophospholipids were inversely associated with advanced stage disease, with risk reduction up to 46% per standard deviation increase in concentration (OR<sub>1SD</sub> = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40-0.72; p <sub>trend</sub> = 0.00004 for PC aa C40:3).
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
reason: The nested case-control study evaluated incident prostate cancer overall and explicitly analyzed advanced-stage disease. The abstract reports 1077 cases and 1077 matched controls but does not state a total analytic N without arithmetic derivation.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Citrulline was associated with a decreased risk of prostate cancer (odds ratio (OR<sub>1SD</sub>) = 0.73; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.62-0.86; p <sub>trend</sub> = 0.0002) in the first 5 years of follow-up after taking multiple testing into account, but not after longer follow-up; results for other metabolites did not vary by time to diagnosis.
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate concerns prostate cancer overall during the first five years after blood collection, not an advanced or otherwise aggressive endpoint.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
